results.reply:
R is the amount risked on one trade — the loss if the stop is hit, used as a single scale to measure trade outcomes against.

Formula: 1R = |entry − stop| × position size

Why it works: measuring results in R lets trades of different sizes and instruments be compared on the same scale — a win of "2R" means twice what was risked, regardless of the dollar size of the position.

In practice: a long BTC trade at entry 77,872, stop 76,580, position size 0.3862 BTC. The stop distance is 1,292 (77,872 − 76,580), so 1R = 1,292 × 0.3862 = $498.97. troid's desk also counts the round-trip fee on a Bitfunded 1-Step (0.04% per side, charged at entry and at the stop): the entry and exit fees together come to $23.86, making the fee-adjusted 1R $522.83.

What this means: on an account sized in this way, 1R is a fixed loss unit — $498.97 before fees, $522.83 with them counted — and every trade's outcome can be read directly in multiples of it.

Sources, each with the date troid read it:
- fee 0.04% per side (Bitfunded 1-Step) — Bitfunded help centre — Criteria to be Success, read 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-23 and 2026-10-04

Tier: the figures above are DERIVED — troid's tools computed them from the rules listed.

Not financial advice. Verify with the firm before acting.
